key_insight: A combinatorial sequential vapor-deposition workflow can independently tune Cs/Pb and Br/Cl compositions to identify wide-bandgap perovskites with high photoluminescence yield, especially within a Cs/Pb window of 1.05–1.20.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable, data-driven route for optimizing optoelectronic perovskite compositions, helping engineers screen large design spaces faster and with better process control.
method: Sequential physical vapor deposition for combinatorial composition control
Automated structural, compositional, and optical characterization
High-throughput screening of >500 sample regions in quaternary Cs-Pb-Br-Cl space
evidence_signal: The abstract reports screening of more than 500 sample regions, which revealed a practical Cs/Pb range of 1.05–1.20 and a high-energy optical transition associated with elevated PL yield.
watch_item: The findings are based on a specific high-throughput vapor-deposition workflow, so translation to other synthesis routes or scale-up conditions may require revalidation.
paper_title: Tuning the optoelectronic properties of wide bandgap perovskites: Data-driven insights from combinatorial synthesis and high-throughput experimentation
